findings.issue: D5 conflicts with ADR-SAG-0013 and the current emitter. The JSONL line is written by the sc-observability v2 sink from a LogEvent envelope: version, timestamp, level, service, target, action, outcome, fields{} (crates/sc-ai/src/observe.rs:144-178). D5 requires flat top-level keys ts, record_version, outcome and so on, with no nested objects. The sink cannot write those without a bespoke JSONL writer, which ADR-0013 forbids. The key 'outcome' also collides with the envelope's own outcome field. Neither D5 nor ADR-0030 says how the record maps onto the envelope (for example the keys live in fields{}, which is nested) or whether ts duplicates the envelope timestamp. The claim 'a sink is the only thing that changes' is unverifiable. SessionEvent/LogEvent in sc-agent-types observability::v2 is on ADR-0027's stable public surface, and its constructor must change (new fields); that is not recorded.
findings.fix: Decide in ADR-SAG-0030: either (a) the record is the envelope fields{} map, and say so with key names that do not collide, or (b) amend 0013 to allow a flat-line sink. Then restate the golden, the SQLite column mapping and the 'no nested objects' rule against that shape. Record the SessionEvent/LogEvent signature change as a stable-surface change under ADR-0027 and 0016.

findings.issue: Unrecorded structural decision: backends 'report' model_id and request_sha256 'alongside the outcome'. The only return path is Result<JudgeOutcome, JevError>. A failed send has no outcome, so there is no channel for these values. D5 declares both NOT NULL, yet r-2b emits a LogEvent for a Failed backend, including digest-recovery or encode failures where nothing was sent and no body exists. This changes the public JudgeOutcome and JudgeBackend contract (judge.rs, test_util MockJudgeBackend, scripted backend). ADR-0009 requires new trait methods to have default bodies. No ADR text covers this, and ADR-SAG-0030 as quoted omits it. This is an owner-level decision (item 5), not a detail.
findings.fix: State in ADR-0030, or in an ADR-0009/0025 amendment, how model_id and request_sha256 reach the emitter on both Ok and Failed (for example a provided-default send-trace on the backend or error side). Resolve nullability: make request_sha256 nullable, or define 'Failed with nothing sent' as writing no record. Reconcile this with the r-2b wording 'a Failed backend emits one LogEvent'.

findings.fix: Either place the main-repo resolver in sc-jev-check beside discover_repo_root, with compose calling it, or amend ADR-0027's enabler list within ADR-SAG-0030. Name the spawn site for the source scan.
